instructions: Trim any thick fat off the lamb and cut it into 3/4 inch pieces. Pat them dry with paper towels and toss them with 1 tsp salt.
Meanwhile, slice the red onion thin and slice the 3 garlic cloves thin. Strip the leaves from 1 rosemary sprig.
Slice both jalapeños into thin rounds and put them in a small bowl for the table. Cut the lemon into 4 wedges.
In a small bowl, stir together 1 tbsp berbere, 1/2 tsp fenugreek, 1/2 tsp ground ginger, 1/4 tsp cardamom, 1/4 tsp cumin and 1/2 tsp black pepper.
Heat a large skillet or wok over high heat for 2 minutes. Add the onion with no fat and stir it for 3 to 4 minutes, until it's soft with a few charred edges. Tip it onto a plate.

Add 1 1/2 tbsp of the ghee to the pan, then half the lamb in a single layer. Leave it alone for 1 minute, until the underside is browned. Toss it and cook for 1 more minute, so the outside is brown and the middle is still pink. Move it to the plate with the onion. Stand back a little. It'll spatter.
Add the last 1 1/2 tbsp ghee and brown the rest of the lamb the same way.
Put all the lamb and onion back in the pan and turn the heat down to medium. Add the garlic, rosemary and the spice mix, and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Tip in the can of tomatoes, breaking them up with your spoon, and pour in 1/3 cup red wine. Scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan.

Let it bubble for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens and coats the lamb. You're cooking the lamb to about 140°F for medium, so if you have a thermometer, check a thick piece. No thermometer? Cut one open: it should be rosy pink in the center, not red.
Take the pan off the heat and squeeze 2 of the lemon wedges over the lamb.
Taste it. If it's flat, add salt first, then a squeeze of lemon.
Serve with injera, the other 2 lemon wedges and the sliced jalapeños on the side.
method_notes: Both versions brown cubed meat hard and fast in a very hot pan, then add berbere, garlic, green chilies and tomato with niter kibbeh or ghee and serve it with injera. Hank Shaw chars the sliced onion in a dry pan first, sears the meat in batches until still rare inside, adds fenugreek, ginger, cardamom, cumin and clove with the berbere, and finishes with tomatoes and red wine for only a minute or two; Sims Home Kitchen simmers chopped fresh tomatoes into a thicker sauce for 7 to 10 minutes and adds rosemary and the kibbeh at the end. This version follows Hank Shaw's quick method and ratios for lamb, takes the rosemary from Sims Home Kitchen, and puts the sliced jalapeños on the table.
